I1.quote: Searched all text and figure pages for a gravimetric, volumetric or flow H2 uptake value on a sorbent; none found. Hydrogen is measured only by TPD: 'The temperature programmed desorption (TPD) apparatus employed to determine the hydrogen capacities'; capacity is read from the desorption peak area, 'corresponds to a hydrogen adsorption capacity of < 1 wt%'. The 'in-house volumetric technique' only confirmed TPD calibrations (CaH2, TiH2, Pd).

I5.quote: The hydrogen storage properties of carbon single-wall and multi-wall nanotubes (SWNTs and MWNTs), graphitic nanofibers, and other nanostructured carbons have recently become the subject of considerable debate.

notes: Only hydrogen measurement is TPD (main p. 2, Experimental Details; Fig. 2, p. 4). The one capacity statement is '< 1 wt%' from the integrated TPD peak for as-synthesized MWNTs (~15 wt% Fe, near ambient). The in-house volumetric technique (main p. 2-3) is cited only to confirm TPD calibration on CaH2, TiH2 and Pd, not as an uptake measurement on a carbon sorbent. No specific surface area was seen anywhere in the text. Not a review, not retracted (is_retracted false), and the paper does not state that its H2 values were published before.
